header_subtitle: Enter your child's weight and age group to calculate correct doses of Acetaminophen (Tylenol) and Ibuprofen (Advil/Motrin) across all formulations.
fever_note_html: When to give fever medication: You may give Tylenol or Advil when your child has a confirmed fever and appears uncomfortable, irritable, or is having difficulty sleeping or eating. A fever alone does not always require medication — it is part of the body's natural immune response. Seek medical attention if: your child is under 3 months with any fever, the fever lasts more than 2–3 days, your child appears very unwell or has difficulty breathing, a febrile seizure occurs, or you are concerned for any reason.
advil_warning_title: Ibuprofen (Advil / Motrin) is NOT safe for infants under 6 months of age
advil_warning_body_html:
Ibuprofen should not be given to any child younger than 6 months old. For fever management in infants under 6 months, Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is the only recommended over-the-counter option — and only with physician guidance for newborns under 3 months of age.

Important: If your infant under 6 months has a fever ≥ 38.0°C (rectal), contact your doctor or go to the emergency department promptly. Fever in young infants can indicate serious infection and requires immediate medical evaluation.
schedule_header: Example Dosing Schedule — Starting at 8:00 AM
sched_staggered_desc: Give Tylenol first, then Advil 3 hours later, and continue alternating. This provides more continuous fever control than either drug alone. Each drug still respects its own minimum interval: Tylenol every 4 h minimum, Advil every 6 h minimum.
sched_tylenol_desc: Use when Advil is unavailable, not tolerated, or your physician recommends Tylenol only. Give every 4 hours as needed (maximum 5 doses in 24 hours).
sched_alternating_desc: Strictly alternating drugs every 4 hours. Each drug is given every 8 hours (well within its maximum frequency). Keep a written log to avoid accidentally doubling a dose.
safety_tylenol_1: Safe from birth (physician guidance for < 3 months)
safety_tylenol_2: Every 4–6 hours as needed; max 5 doses/24 h
safety_tylenol_5: Check cold/flu combination products for hidden acetaminophen
safety_advil_2: Every 6–8 hours as needed; max 4 doses/24 h
safety_advil_4: Give with food or milk to reduce stomach upset
safety_advil_5: Avoid if dehydrated, or with kidney or bleeding problems
footer_html: Disclaimer: This sheet is a clinical reference aid. Doses are based on standard weight-based guidelines (acetaminophen 15 mg/kg/dose; ibuprofen 10 mg/kg/dose). Individual patient factors including age, organ function, concurrent medications, and clinical context must always be considered. Verify with current formulary guidelines (e.g. CPS, SickKids Drug Handbook). This tool does not replace clinical judgment. Formulations listed are representative Canadian market products — always confirm label concentration before dispensing.
warn_under5kg: ⚠️ Weight < 5 kg detected — if this child is under 6 months, please toggle the age group above. Ibuprofen is contraindicated under 6 months.
